name: Gerk
slug: Gerk is a half-orc barbarian Doorman and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree who opens Arch doorways and keeps the Midgard keystone.
description: Gerk is a half-orc barbarian and party ambassador who has been revealed as a Child of the Great Eldarin Tree and the child foretold by the Mother’s Prayer. He serves as the Doorman, a unique role that allows him to open, close, connect with, and protect Arch doorways. Gerk is the keeper of the Midgard keystone and is entrusted with helping make Midgard greater rather than simply concealing its power. His developing ability to create seamless doorways through reality is still difficult to control, particularly their destinations, but he is learning to use this power. As a Child of the Tree and honorary member of the Navi, Gerk's path is connected to prophecy while his choices remain his own.

log.summary: Gerk was confirmed as the surviving child foretold by the Mother’s Prayer and one of the Children of the Great Eldarin Tree. He accepted the unique role of **Doorman**, gaining the ability to open, close, and protect Arch doorways, and chose the **Midgard keystone**, taking responsibility for using it to help make Midgard greater rather than simply hiding it. Gerk was formally welcomed as a Child of the Tree and honorary member of the Navi. He began experimenting with his new power to create seamless doorways through reality, successfully reaching an unknown beach, a rainy gray mountainside, and a forest near Langdale, though he could not yet control where the portals lead and failed to reach the Great Hall of the Stronghold. The DM warned him that closing a portal may make returning to the exact same location difficult and that portals should not be left unattended. Gerk also saw the mysterious white-flower girl and became interested in following her trail.
notes: Confirmed as the child foretold by the Mother's Prayer and one of the children of the Great Eldarin Tree.
Sylan's meditation in Jotunheim identified Gerk as the surviving child referenced in Sylan's journal and as a keeper who would open doors.
Gerk initially questioned whether the prophecy uniquely identified him, but accepted the responsibility after learning that doing so could help all of Atlas.
The prophecy describes Gerk's path but does not dictate his choices; his decisions remain his own.
The Mother's Prayer's stipulations involve Gerk's companions, allowing them to join him as metaphorical brothers and sisters of the Tree.
Gerk was formally welcomed as a Child of the Tree and honorary member of the Navi.
Gerk accepted the unique title of Doorman, distinct from the other party members' Gatekeeper roles.
As Doorman, Gerk can open and close Arch doorways, connect with them, and protect them.
Gerk chose the Midgard keystone and became responsible for protecting, using, and helping make Midgard greater rather than merely hiding its keystone.
Gerk can create seamless doorways through reality by grasping an invisible handle.
His first doorway led to an unknown beach on Midgard; subsequent attempts reached a rainy gray mountainside and a forest near Langdale.
Gerk currently cannot reliably control the destination of his doorways and failed to deliberately reach the Great Hall of the Stronghold.
The DM warned that closing a portal may make reopening it to the exact same location difficult and advised Gerk not to leave portals unattended.
Gerk can see the mysterious white-flower girl and wants to follow her trail.
Gerk is experimenting with his new portal abilities and is beginning to learn how to operate them.

log.summary: Gerk is confirmed as the Doorman responsible for calibrating and properly seating keystones before safe activation, becoming the party’s primary assistance for operating the gatehouse. He experiments with his door-opening ability, first connecting to unknown environments and later opening a doorway to Mahali’s stronghold by concentrating on a desired location. Using the ability from the moving ship causes severe spatial distortion, stretching the ship and surrounding reality toward the stationary doorway and exerting dangerous forces on Gerk. He takes responsibility for closing the doorway despite believing doing so may be fatal. Afterward, Gerk fails a Wisdom saving throw and is affected by confusion, becoming incoherent and unable to move or act normally. A giant, shiny spectral door resembling his shield in door form appears above him. Gerk becomes unseen while remaining physically tangible, allowing Sylan to locate and support him despite being unable to see him. Gerk can still move his mouth and scream, but his voice cannot be heard, while an unseen force manipulates his body and Sylan drags him toward the spectral door.
notes: Gerk is confirmed as the doorman and overseer responsible for the gates at this particular gatehouse.
The doorman must help orient and calibrate the keystones and ensure they are properly seated before safe activation.
With Plymouth accompanying Walker, Gerk becomes the party's primary source of assistance for operating the keystones at the gatehouse.
As Doorman, Gerk is responsible for calibrating and properly seating keystones before the gates can be safely activated.
Gerk begins experimenting with his new gate-opening ability and successfully opens multiple portals to unknown environments.
His first attempt releases a large quantity of brackish swamp water; his second reveals a hot, sulfurous wasteland with geysers.
With Plymouth leaving the gatehouse, Gerk becomes the sole remaining party member responsible for helping operate the keystones.

His first demonstrated portal opened onto brackish swamp water and produced a powerful rush of water.
A second portal opened onto a barren, arid landscape with geysers, steam, intense heat, and sulfuric/brimstone smells.
He is beginning to experiment with controlling where and how the portals open and intends to practice during the voyage.
He plans to test whether concentrating on a familiar location, such as the party's house, can cause a portal to open there.
Continues experimenting with his door-opening ability while traveling.
Can attempt to open a doorway to a specific familiar location, including his own house and bedroom.
Opening a door from a moving boat can cause the surrounding space and part of the boat to stretch outward while the boat continues moving normally.
The doorway can exert a strong pulling force on Gerk, requiring a Strength saving throw if he attempts to hold onto it.
Successfully uses his Doorman ability to open a doorway to another location while aboard the moving ship.
The ability can apparently target a place through concentration or intention rather than requiring a conventional physical doorway.
Opening the door while the ship is moving causes the ship and surrounding material to stretch toward the stationary doorway.
Gerk rolls a 31 on a Strength saving throw and is able to hold onto the doorway despite the extreme forces involved.
Gerk experiences passage through the doorway as movement through time and space with a thick, resistant sensation.
The doorway remains open after Gerk passes through instead of closing automatically.
Gerk identifies himself to Mahali as the Doorman.
Demonstrated his Doorkeeper ability by opening a doorway to Mahali's stronghold while aboard the moving ship.
His doorway appears capable of connecting directly to a desired location if he concentrates on it.
Using the doorway while the ship was moving caused the ship and surrounding reality to stretch or behave like a rubber band.
Gerk believes closing the doorway may have dangerous consequences and is willing to remain aboard the ship to face them.
He was physically pulled through the doorway by Mahali after becoming stranded while the ship moved away.
Believes closing the door may be dangerous enough to kill him because he caused the distortion.
Recognizes that movement while using the door appears to stretch reality and may cause the ship to occupy multiple positions.
Takes responsibility for closing the door and prepares to do so despite the risk.
Feels the temporal or dimensional barrier again immediately before closing the door.
Rolls a 5 on a d10 during the resolution of the door's effects.
Gerk takes responsibility for stepping through and closing the door.
Gerk rolls a d10 to resolve the door's effect and gets a 5.
Gerk is treated by Sylan as the party member specifically suited to handling the doors because of his Doorman role.
Sylan suggests that Gerk's role as Doorman means he was specifically meant to deal with the current magical door situation.
Gerk failed the Wisdom saving throw associated with the magical effect.
Gerk was affected by a confusion spell after the door closed and became unable to move or take actions.
A giant spectral door appeared near the location where Gerk had been.
The magical event is centered on Gerk and the Doorman aspect of his power.
Gerk fails the Wisdom saving throw and is immediately affected by a confusion effect.
While confused, Gerk is unable to meaningfully move or take actions and cannot understand what is happening.
A giant spectral door appears near where Gerk had been after the magical discharge.
The spectral door resembles Gerk's door when it is in shield form.
Gerk is still incoherent and unable to understand what is happening during the separation.
Gerk cannot normally move during this phenomenon, although the DM allows him to fall to the floor.
Sylan can physically locate and support Gerk despite being unable to see him.
A spectral door appears near Gerk and resembles Gerk's door when his shield is in door form.
Gerk is affected by the strange invisibility/disappearance phenomenon and cannot be seen even though he remains physically present.
Gerk appears unable to move normally while affected, although the DM permits him to fall to the ground by giving up his attempt to remain standing.
Gerk remains physically tangible: Sylan can collide with, strike, support, and shake him despite being unable to see him.
A very shiny spectral door is hovering above Gerk while he is affected by the phenomenon.
Gerk is currently being affected by an unseen force that shakes and moves him despite his apparent inability to move normally.
A shiny spectral door is hovering above Gerk while he is being manipulated.
Gerk can physically move his mouth and scream, but his voice is not heard by the surrounding party members.
Sylan is able to physically reposition Gerk's head and drag his body toward the spectral door.

log.summary: Gerk remains aboard the invisible, silent boat while suffering under a confusion effect, reacting to unseen hands until Sylan physically wrangles him and he grows slightly more lucid. After failing a wisdom save with a natural one and trying to swing Sylan, he admits through blind eye speech that he opened the door. With guidance he investigates the spectral door for a total of eighteen, identifying it as fake protective magic he can pass through but not manipulate physically. He refuses Ord's proposal to create a replacement door, is blamed for opening a doorway on the moving boat, and accepts the lesson not to open doors while underway. The spectral door now follows him aboard ship, resisting dismissal by command, performance, or "closed sesame," until he agrees not to open another door until landfall. He also suggests giving Mikkel a teleportation tunnel or other means to rejoin the boat.
notes: Remains on the invisible, silent party boat under the confusion effect.
Feels accosted by unseen hands, grabs back, and becomes slightly more lucid.
Fails a wisdom save with a natural 1 and tries to swing Sylan around during the struggle.
Admits through blind eye speech that he opened the door.
Investigates the spectral door with guidance for a total of 18 and identifies it as fake protective magic.
Cannot physically interact with the spectral door beyond passing through it.
Refuses to listen to Ord's suggestion to create a replacement door and briefly proposes leaving through a new magic door instead.
Is blamed for causing the doorway incident on the moving boat.
Accepts the lesson not to open doors on moving things.
The spectral door now follows him, staying near him as he moves and fixed on the ship when it sails.
Waving, commands, closed sesame, and a 17 performance check fail to dismiss it.
Agrees not to open another door until the party reaches land.
Suggests giving Mikkel a teleportation tunnel or other way back to the boat.

log.summary: Gerk sees the spectral door following him, refuses to touch it on the boat, and agrees to keep sailing and report if anything changes. When it vanishes after about a day, he feels briefly more vulnerable, then the feeling fades. He checks a watch to judge whether twelve or twenty-four hours have passed, though he has trouble reading it. With Sylan, Dana, and Ord he goes to Carlkin’s lighthouse in New Navel, reads a posted notice as “Knock loud. Be let in,” and knocks hard enough to crack the boards and throw the door open. Sylan introduces him as the party’s ambassador; he points out Sylan’s arms and walks in when Carlkin tries to push him out. He opens a door with no destination chosen and rolls the abyss, telling Carlkin he can open doors anywhere but does not know how the power works. A tentacle grapples him about the waist. He peeks through, succeeds on a Wisdom save, sees thousands of eyes—one pupil shaped like a small light-complexioned figure—and tells the others not to look. He rages and takes a legendary tentacle hit before Ord severs it. He does not close the door, then breaks the cobbles under Ord and holds him in a hole so Ord cannot continue through.
notes: He can see the spectral door following him, refuses to touch it on the boat, and agrees to keep sailing and report if anything changes. When it vanishes after about a day, he feels briefly more vulnerable, then the feeling fades.
He checks a watch to judge whether twelve or twenty-four hours have passed. He has trouble reading it; the watch does move.

He goes with Sylan, Dana, and Ord to Carlkin's lighthouse in New Navel. He says he can read and reads a posted notice as "Knock loud. Be let in." He knocks hard enough to crack the boards and throw the door open, rolling a 12 and treating it as a 32 Strength check. Sylan introduces him as the party's ambassador. He answers Carlkin by pointing out Sylan's arms and walks in when Carlkin tries to push him out.

In the living room he opens a door with no destination chosen, slowly in case water comes out, and rolls 68 on a d100. The opening is the abyss. He tells Carlkin he can open doors anywhere but does not know how the power works.

A tentacle grapples him about the waist. He is grappled with movement 0, and escaping costs his action. He had not drawn a weapon. He peeks through, succeeds on a Wisdom save of 24, sees thousands of eyes, nearly loses himself, and tells the others not to look. One pupil is shaped like a small light-complexioned figure.

His Charisma bonus is +5 to ability checks and saves, and Sentinel applies to his initiative. He rolls 19 and his initiative is 25 after Ord's proficiency bonus. He rages as a bonus action and takes 9 bludgeoning from a legendary tentacle attack of 24. Ord later severs the tentacle holding him.
Adjacent to the wall of eyes, he succeeds on a Wisdom save of 23 (18 plus his +5). He suggests opening a second door so the doors fight, or going three doors down. He does not close this door.

He breaks the cobbles under Ord with his hammer (attack 15, 16 damage), then on a Strength check of 27 dives about five feet under the floor and holds Ord in the hole so Ord cannot continue through the door.

log.summary: Gerk opened doors twice, once with no destination and once aboard the moving sky ship; the lighthouse door went between the arches, and he was relieved the creature does not live there. He failed to level the cobbles a doorway broke, leaving a hole and piles like sandcastles, and kept admiring the damage until Carlkin ordered him off it; Carlkin will repair it with Mending. Asked if his mother is dead, he cried. Carlkin and Sylan treat him as an orphan. He said people never asked, described a blonde girl with flowers, and looked for a daisy in his hair. He said nobody taught him the rules and he would have avoided the responsibility if he had known. Carlkin said the legends treat the role as Gerk's choice; Gerk said Sylan agreed and first identified him as the Doorman. He believes Plymouth was present when he received the ability and never explained the rules; Carlkin agrees Plymouth did not teach the dangers. Gerk claims he cannot write. At the word agenda he lay on the floor. He was told others can open doors, but their names were withheld. Carlkin calls him a footman, an apprentice rank, until he earns Doorman; Gerk accepts grudgingly and promises not to open a door in Carlkin's home again. He is described as changed or bound to a keystone, which Carlkin expects future portals to follow. Sylan says he is still the only party member who can open a door. Carlkin's detect magic does not treat that door as a magical item. Asked which path he had picked, Gerk recounted his day and feelings; Grixto did not like it.
notes: Opened doors twice in the day, including once with no destination. One was aboard the moving sky ship. The lighthouse door went between the arches. He is relieved the creature does not live there.

Tried and failed to level the cobbles the doorway broke, leaving a hole and cobbles piled like sandcastles. He keeps admiring the damage until Carlkin orders him off it. Carlkin will repair it with Mending.
Asked if his mother is dead, he cries. Carlkin and Sylan treat him as an orphan. He says people never asked. He describes a blonde girl with flowers and looks for a daisy in his hair.

Says nobody taught him the rules and that he would have avoided the responsibility if he had known. Carlkin says the legends treat the role as Gerk's own choice. Gerk says Sylan agreed to it and knows how he is. Sylan, not Gerk, first identified him as the Doorman.
Believes Plymouth was present when he received the ability, knows the rules, and never explained them. Carlkin agrees Plymouth was there and did not teach the dangers.
Claims he cannot write. Carlkin still wants the lesson written down. At the word agenda, Gerk lies down on the floor.
Asks whether other people can open doors and whether Carlkin knows every doorman. He is told that others can; the names are withheld.
Carlkin withholds Doorman and calls him a footman, an apprentice rank, until he earns it. Gerk accepts the label grudgingly and promises never to open a door in Carlkin's home again.

Described as changed or bound to one of the keystones. Carlkin expects future portals from him to be tied to that stone. Sylan says Gerk is still the only one of the party who can open a door. Carlkin's detect magic does not treat that door as a magical item.
When Grixto asked which path he had picked, Gerk answered with a long account of his day, his feelings, and his well-being. Grixto did not like it.

log.summary: Gerk keeps tapping the lighthouse floor level by hand after Carlkin tells him to stop, and takes the blame when his request for help goes unheard. He is both Doorman and gatekeeper: his doors come from nothing, need no keystone, open and close from either side, and only he can shut them. He refuses even ordinary doors and climbs out a window until Carlkin clarifies that he meant the doorway ability; Gerk had already opened doors to get the party inside and will not take that risk again. The thing on his arm is the last memory of his mother. Being told to put that door down, and that his mother will not come through the portal, pushes him to rage; he cries, babbles, is dragged out, and says he may punch Carlkin one day. After the pub with Sylan and Ord he accepts Sylan as trainer and asks Ord to come. He will not practice in the living room after a portal toward hell, wants somewhere remote, and goes south into the forest with Sylan, Ord, and Ciri. He will not trigger the ability by being made angry, though he later rages and forces one opening. Aiming for the upstairs hallway of the Twin Peaks tavern, which he remembers better than Volga, by focusing a respectful distance from his best friend just seen, confusion shifts the door to the barn loft where he has slept, including the levitated donkey or mule; he shuts it before anyone falls through. He refuses a key on or near him, will not try a doorway to Sylan’s sister after failing to reach Ciri, and can feel an open door and its far end without knowing the magic or how close he can place one. He shuts the battlefield door at once, cuts the tomato plant free, holds the shut door while something rams it, then lets go rather than reopen it, and rides home instead of portaling to the stronghold.
notes: Still trying to repair the lighthouse hole after Carlkin told him to stop, tapping the floor level by hand. He had asked for help in his own way, Carlkin did not listen, and Gerk takes the blame as his fault.

He is both Doorman and gatekeeper. His doors come from nothing and need no keystone. He can open and close one from either side, and only he can shut it. Carlkin floats joke titles: gate doorman, door-gate man, and portcullis man.

After the warning he refuses even ordinary doors and climbs out a window. Carlkin clarifies that he meant the doorway ability. Gerk had already opened doors to get the party inside and will not take that risk again.

The thing on his arm is, to him, the last memory of his mother. Carlkin telling him to put that door down, and saying his mother will not come through the portal, pushes him to rage. He cries, babbles, and has to be dragged out. He says he may punch Carlkin one day.

He goes to the pub with Sylan and Ord. After breakfast he accepts Sylan as trainer and asks Ord to come. He will not practice in the living room after previously opening a portal toward hell, prefers somewhere remote, and does not care whether the ground is dirt or stone. There is no island in the stronghold lake. He goes south into the forest with Sylan, Ord, and Ciri.

He will not trigger the ability by being made angry, though he later rages and forces one opening. He says he is poor at vivid place descriptions but willing to practice. He describes the accurate door to Sylan as focusing on a respectful distance from his best friend, helped by having just seen him and knowing his general location.

He remembers Twin Peaks, including friends, better than Volga, and aims for the upstairs hallway of the tavern rather than the busy street. Confusion shifts that opening to the barn loft, a place he has slept, including the memory of the levitated donkey or mule. He shuts it before anyone falls through.
He refuses to have a key put on or near him and says he will not fall for that trick again. He will not try a doorway to Sylan's sister after the failed reach toward Ciri.

He can feel a door he has opened and the presence of its far end. He does not know what magic the door uses or how close he can place one. He shuts the battlefield door at once, cuts the tomato plant free, holds the shut door while something rams it, then lets go rather than reopen it onto the growling thing. He rides home instead of portaling to the stronghold.

log.summary: Gerk practices doorways from different directions while Ciri throws rocks and says the Doorman ability seems fine after Sylan pushed him to rein it in. Someone adept has helped, but he will not say if he has always had the ability. His heat stone is a hot rock he puts in his pants; a loose primal stone cannot make fire until set in an object that releases energy. Ord's strength lost to the Grunkle is hidden inside him, and restoration or greater restoration cannot return it, because you cannot restore what is not missing. Sylan remembered the uncle punching it out of him. Within 30 feet of the lantern he fails a Wisdom save totaling 8. Blinded, he hears spirits sucked in, considers a door to light, and stays blind through the beacon and aftermath, whirling his hammer without attacking, terrified his eyes are all he has. Tremorsense feels an approach; he suspects a mimic, and his only note is that he does not trust the cat man. He touches Sylan's face. Lesser restoration restores his sight. He hugs and lifts Sylan, asks what they did to his eyes, and, having heard voices before, is furious Sylan haunted him. He tells Sylan to do the New Navel ghost work at Carlkin's house.
notes: Practices doorways by opening them from different directions while Ciri throws rocks at him. He says the day of training is going well and the Doorman ability seems fine. Sylan had pushed him to rein the ability in. He says someone has been adept at helping with his doorway problems, and that the recent help has been useful. He does not answer whether he has had the ability the entire time.

Returns to the tavern with the others and has nothing special planned there. He treats his heat stone as a hot rock he puts in his pants. A loose primal stone would not let him create fire; it has to be set into an object that releases the energy.

The strength Ord lost to the Grunkle is hidden inside Gerk. Restoration and greater restoration cannot return it. The clue is that you cannot restore what is not missing. Sylan first remembered the uncle punching the strength out of Gerk.

Stays at the door-testing spot in the shade and watches the lantern trial. Within 30 feet he looks toward the light and fails a Wisdom save: 3 plus about +5 from Ord's nearby ward, total 8, against a DC that must break 10. He is blinded, on the ground, and can hear the spirits being sucked in. He considers opening a door to light.

He remains blind through the beacon and the aftermath, screaming and whirling his hammer overhead to keep things away. He is not moving to attack. He says he is terrified and that his eyes are all he has. He will not stop.

Tremorsense lets him feel someone approaching. He suspects a mimic and demands proof. The one note he has written down is 'I don't trust the cat man.' He holds the hammer ready in one hand and reaches with the other to touch Sylan's face.

Lesser restoration restores his sight. He recognizes Sylan, hugs him, and lifts him up, then asks what they did to his eyes. He has had voices in his head before and is furious at the idea Sylan haunted him. He says he cannot afford to be haunted. He tells Sylan to do the New Navel ghost work at Carlkin's house.

log.summary: The fused lantern-staff blinds Gerk again apart from Ord and Sylan. Unsure he was looking at it, he wants compensation and does not want to be cursed. He does not want to investigate the New Navel spirits but goes with Sylan. Door training has improved a little, though he still needs work. Elrus offers to train his mind, calling him strong of body and lacking in mind. Abyss doors happen when he thinks of nothing, not whenever he fails to be quiet. Dana bars him and Sylan from Carlkin: no doors to nothing dimensions, no abyssal monsters, and no doors in moving vehicles. He warns Carlkin is in a bad way. He stays in the sword realm, stacking rocks through foggy Sylan. He asks the sheriff to announce that spirits who want to move on should find Sylan. He buys Joanna's wicker chicken for one gold and jokes about geese, later mostly in jest. He asks Haldor to send bad spirits on and says the Carlkin door was extradimensional. Haldor bans town doors and files him as a hooligan. Gerk will keep his dragon friend away. He thinks Carlkin wants an arrest, unconfirmed. Carlkin forbids the emperor's helm; Sylan agrees.
notes: The fused lantern-staff blinds him again while he is apart from Ord and Sylan. He is not sure he was looking at it. He takes the blinding personally and wants compensation. He does not want to be cursed and does not want to investigate the New Navel spirits, but he goes with Sylan anyway.
Door training has improved enough that he can manipulate doors a little better. He still needs work. Elrus offers to train his mind and calls him strong of body and lacking in mind.

He does not meditate and says he does not have a quiet mind. Abyss doors happen when he thinks about nothing, not whenever he fails to be quiet. He thinks raging while opening a door would go poorly. On a seventeen-foot door he tried to open it harder.

He does not want to become physically larger, because he barely fits places as he is. He already knew Elrus has an ancient dragon and did not know Elrus's height. He treats the oak-sapling remark as a possible insult until Elrus explains it.
Dana bars him and Sylan from the Carlkin visit, with no doors to nothing dimensions, no abyssal monsters, and no doors in moving vehicles. He warns that Carlkin is in a bad way.

He stays with Sylan during the sword-realm visit, stacks rocks that fall through the translucent Sylan, and rings Sylan's feet with stones. He is curious and a little tempted by a later visit. He keeps busy collecting ordinary rocks and notices that Sylan looked foggy.

Sylan sends him into New Navel to find the sheriff and ask for an announcement that spirits who want to move on should find Sylan. He is uneasy about identifying harmful spirits if Sylan is outside town, and about how anyone arrests something that is simply drawn into Sylan.

He asks directions in the market, buys a wicker chicken from Joanna for one gold, refuses a wicker goose, and tells the goose vendor two doors down that he will be back. He says killing geese on sight is a religious obligation and calls them evil little birds. He later says the threat was mostly in jest. He has not killed the wicker creatures; Sylan offers to buy the others he mentioned.
He finds Haldor on the porch, waves, and asks him to help send bad spirits on. He explains the jug image, bad spirits going into Sylan so they can be sent home, and leaves the real account to Sylan.

He says yesterday's Carlkin door was supposed to be interdimensional, that he did not know it would be extradimensional, that he fixed the floor, and that they will apologize. He practiced doors today in a clearing away from people. He does not have interdimensional shackles and is told not to open a door to them.
He walked back from Trigash with Sylan while the others flew. Haldor has not seen him in some time and includes him in the stronghold hooligans file.

Haldor forbids doors in town and tells him to keep commotion outside town. Gerk jokes that he will use only windows, and Haldor shuts the joke down. Gerk understands the order as staying out of town and keeping his dragon friend away from the ghosts.

He thinks Carlkin wants the party arrested. That is not confirmed. Carlkin separately forbids him from ever wearing the emperor's helm, because a minor soul fragment would be dangerous in a feeble-minded wearer and because the helm is the emperor's. Sylan agrees he should not wear it.

openQuestions: Who is Daisy, and what is her connection to Gerk?
What exactly does being a Child of the Great Eldarin Tree entail?
What additional abilities and responsibilities does the Doorman role provide?
Can Gerk eventually control the destinations of his doorways?
How difficult will it be to reopen a portal to a previously visited exact location?
What does Gerk ultimately become by fully taking on the keeper mantle?
